Cloud cover is broken (62% cloud fraction) and an afternoon thunderstorm threat (40% PoP after 1pm) introduces meaningful downside risk to afternoon heating. The day is tracking on the warmer side of expectations given the early-afternoon temperature already at 84°F, but the incoming storm window may constrain further gains.
forecast_obs_notes: Models diverge significantly: ECMWF (83.8°F) is now essentially at the current observed temperature, suggesting it may already be verifying or slightly under-forecasting, while HRRR (89.8°F) and the NWS narrative (near 89°F) expect continued strong afternoon warming. max_temp_prediction: With the current temp at 84.2°F and a predicted peak near 14.5h ET (~2:30 PM), a simple extrapolation at the current +1.8°F/hr warming rate yields roughly 87–88°F before the rate naturally slackens near peak. The META model, which is the most reliable fused signal, assigns its highest probability to the 88–89°F bucket (29.6%) with meaningful weight also on 90–91°F and 86–87°F. Confidence is moderate: the HRRR/NWS consensus near 89–90°F would verify if storms are delayed until late afternoon, but an early storm arrival (pre-2 PM) consistent with ECMWF's cooler solution could cap the high closer to 85–86°F. Best estimate is 87.5°F, reflecting the balance between the observed warming trajectory and the afternoon convective risk.
